label: rejected

evidence.V1: Stacked faceted strata with a mossy cap read as a cliff/rock chunk in front and three-quarter; silhouette shows distinct stepped ledges; bottom-origin and seated (all strata seated, no gaps).
evidence.V2: Big strata slabs and medium designed facets are clear, but there is almost no small tier: the only secondary read is the moss top, with no chips, cracks or pebbles.
evidence.V3: Slab stack is partly stylised, but the second stratum is sunk into the one below (0.26 stud penetration) leaving a thin sliver lip and a wedge-shaped dark slit that looks accidental rather than designed; strata are similar thickness so the stack reads a bit uniform.
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with consistently softened edges that catch light across all strata.
evidence.V5: Strata close-up (flat and studio) shows a thin wedge/sliver where stratum 2 intersects stratum 1, reading as a pinched crevice; otherwise facets shade cleanly.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values plus a single leaf-green moss secondary; colourways (sandstone, redrock) keep the structure.
evidence.V7: 538 tris vs medium target 2000 (ceiling 4000): well under target.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, designed rock facets, stone hue + moss green secondary per the Nature kit; moss green is slightly saturated but within the scheme.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Hull (Box per stratum option), CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, bottom-centre origin.

artifacts: Wedge-shaped sliver / slit where stratum 2 is sunk into stratum 1 (front strata close-up)
top_fixes: Re-seat stratum 2 so it rests on stratum 1 with a clean overhang instead of sinking in and leaving a thin sliver/slit
Vary strata thickness and add a small tier (chipped corners, a crack line, a pebble or moss drip down one face)
Let the moss spill a little over the top edge so it reads as growth rather than a painted cap
